title: Open-weight vs closed AI models: what the difference means for you
summary: Open-weight models can be downloaded and run anywhere; closed models live behind an API. The trade-offs on cost, control, capability and risk.
body:
A **closed** model (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable, Gemini) is reachable only through its vendor's API. An **open-weight** model (Meta's Llama family, Mistral's open releases, DeepSeek, Google's Gemma, OpenAI's gpt-oss, Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small, Meituan's LongCat-2.5) publishes the trained parameters so anyone can download, run, modify and redistribute it under a licence.

"Open-weight" is not the same as "open source": the weights are public but the training data and full recipe usually are not. The licence varies too, from Apache 2.0 and MIT to community licences with use restrictions; see [open-source AI licences explained](/learn/open-source-ai-licenses-explained/).

## Why companies choose open weights

- **Control.** Run it in your own data center or cloud account. No data leaves. No vendor can change or retire the model under you.
- **Cost at scale.** Above a certain volume, renting GPUs and running an open model is cheaper than paying per token.
- **Customisation.** Fine-tune on your own data without restrictions.
- **No rate limits or outages you do not control.**

## Why companies choose closed

- **Capability.** The top closed models still lead on the hardest reasoning and agentic tasks, though the gap narrows every few months.
- **No operations.** No GPUs to provision, no serving stack to maintain, no security patches for inference servers. Inkling 2 Small's November 2026 weights release needed 500 GB of VRAM and a development build of vLLM or SGLang on day one; that is the operations bill in one line.
- **Features.** Tool use, caching, batch, long context and safety tooling arrive first on the vendor API.

## The security angle

Open weights can be audited and run air-gapped, which regulated industries like. They can also be fine-tuned by anyone to remove safety behaviour, which is why dual-use capability such as advanced cyber-offence tends to ship closed and gated (OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber and Anthropic's Mythos line are available only to vetted customers).

## A practical rule

Prototype on a closed API for speed. Once a workload is stable and large, price out an open model on your own infrastructure for that specific task. Many companies end up with both: closed for the hard, low-volume tasks and open for the high-volume, well-defined ones.
faqs: The weights are free to download under their licence, but running them costs compute, and some licences restrict commercial use above a size threshold.
It changes monthly. The model release tracker lists new open releases with links to the vendor's page.
Is my data safer with open models?
It never leaves your infrastructure, which removes one class of risk. You then own every other class: access control, patching, and monitoring.
